claim: Alba is nicknamed the 'City of a Hundred Towers' for the family towers built in the Middle Ages as symbols of wealth, of which only a few survive including the Torre Astesiano which offers panoramic views.
quote: City of a Hundred Towers ... numerous family towers were erected in the Middle Ages as symbols of wealth and power ... Torre Astesiano ... one of the few remaining medieval towers

claim: The tallest surviving medieval towers in Alba are the Torre Sineo (about 35m) and Torre Bonino (about 30m), with the 17th-century Torre Parussa, the 19th-century Torre Ravinale and the 12th/13th-century Torre Artesiana also standing near Piazza del Duomo.
quote: Torre Bonino, Torre Astesiano and Torre Sieno, located in Piazza del Duomo ... Torre Sineo (35 meters high) and the Torre Bonino (approximately 30 metres high) ... 17th century Torre Parussa (approximately 21 metres), the 19th century Torre Ravinale and the 12th/13th century Torre Artesiana

claim: Alba's Cathedral of San Lorenzo was radically rebuilt in the 15th-16th centuries over an earlier Romanesque and Early Christian basilica; its highlight is the 1512 wooden choir by Bernardino Fossati of Codogno with 35 stalls inlaid with still lifes and fantasy landscapes, plus a bell tower whose core is late 10th-early 11th century.
quote: Wooden Choir (1512): Created by Bernardino Fossati of Codogno ... 35 stalls illustrate still lifes and fantasy landscapes ... Bell Tower ... older (late 10th-early 11th century) version within a 12th-century structure

claim: The Cathedral of San Lorenzo overlooks Piazza Risorgimento with a rugged red-brick Piedmontese facade (three doors, central rose window, four pointed turrets) and a Gothic interior of three naves in gold and blue with a starry-sky vault and six side chapels.
quote: rugged red-brick exterior that is quintessentially Piedmontese, while the Gothic interior surprises with a luminous palette of gold and blue across its three aisles ... three entrance doors ... central rose window and the four pointed roof turrets ... starry sky vault

claim: The MUDI Diocesan Museum is set in the underground chambers beneath the Cathedral and runs an archaeological path through Romanesque, Gothic and Renaissance artifacts including the Coat of Arms Room and Saint Peter's Crypt, with excavations (2007-2011) revealing remains of the Roman city of Alba Pompeia.
quote: located in the underground chambers of Saint Lawrence Cathedral and features an archaeological path ... from the Coat of Arms Room to Saint Peter's Crypt ... remains of the Roman city of Alba Pompeia

claim: The 'Underground Alba' (Alba Sotterranea) guided walking tours depart from Piazza Risorgimento and take roughly 1.5-2 hours across three underground Roman archaeological sites, ending with free entry to the 20-room Eusebio civic museum.
quote: Underground Alba walking tours depart from Piazza Risorgimento n. 1 or 2, Alba (also called Piazza del Duomo) ... approximately one and a half to two hours ... three underground archaeological sites, with free visit to the 20 rooms of the 'Eusebio' museum

claim: Via Vittorio Emanuele, known locally as Via Maestra, is Alba's main pedestrian street, crossing the entire old town and ending at the arcaded Piazza Savona, with San Domenico a late-12th-century early-Gothic church a few minutes' walk from the Cathedral.
quote: Via Vittorio Emanuele, which its inhabitants affectionately call Via Maestra ... crosses the entire old town and ends in Piazza Savona ... Church of San Domenico was built in the late 12th Century in early Gothic style

claim: The small church of Santa Maria Maddalena, tucked into Via Vittorio Emanuele in central Alba, was designed by Piedmontese Baroque architect Bernardo Vittone and completed in 1749, with an altar holding the body of Blessed Margherita of Savoy since 1464.
quote: designed by the prominent Piedmontese architect Bernardo Vittone, and completed in 1749 ... altar is dedicated to Blessed Margherita of Savoy, whose body has rested here since 1464
